title: Question 1
statement_text: Is it true that for every planar graph $H$, Max Independent Set can be solved in polynomial time in the class of graphs excluding $H$ as an induced minor?
context_text: Dallard, Milanič, and Štorgel [JCTB '24] explicitly posed this question, asking whether MIS admits a polynomial-time algorithm across all planar induced-minor-free graph classes. Currently no polynomial-time algorithm is known even when $H$ is the 7-vertex path, illustrating the depth of the problem.
paper_contribution: Proves a polynomial-time algorithm running in $n^{O(t^{5})}$ for MIS in graphs excluding $K_{1}+tK_{2}$ as an induced minor, settling Question 1 for this infinite family of planar graphs.
notes: Attribution to Dallard–Milanič–Štorgel is explicit in the abstract; corresponds to reference [25] (JCTB 2024).
paper_title: Maximum Independent Set when excluding an induced minor: $K_1 + tK_2$ and $tC_3 \uplus C_4$

title: Question 2
statement_text: Is it true that for every planar graph $H$, Max Independent Set can be solved in quasipolynomial time in the class of graphs excluding $H$ as an induced minor?
context_text: A graph $H$ is an induced minor of $G$ if $H$ can be obtained from $G$ by vertex deletions and edge contractions; $G$ is $H$-induced-minor-free otherwise. Max Independent Set asks for a maximum-size independent set; quasipolynomial time means time $n^{(\log n)^{O(1)}}$. $G_1\uplus G_2$ is the disjoint union, $tG$ the disjoint union of $t$ copies of $G$, $C_t$ the cycle on $t$ vertices. For non-planar $H$ the problem is NP-complete on $H$-induced-minor-free graphs, since they include all planar graphs; no planar $H$ is known for which it is NP-complete. Dallard, Milanič and Štorgel asked whether for every planar $H$ the problem is solvable in polynomial time on $H$-induced-minor-free graphs, which is open even for $H=P_7$; the present question is its quasipolynomial relaxation, for which more is known: quasipolynomial algorithms exist for $H=C_t$ (Gartland et al.) and $H=tC_3$ (Bonamy et al.), and Korhonen gave a $2^{O(n/\log^c n)}$-time algorithm for every planar $H$ (impossible in general graphs under ETH). The paper adds a polynomial $n^{O(t^5)}$ algorithm for the friendship graph $K_1+tK_2$ and a quasipolynomial $n^{O(t^2\log n)+f(t)}$ algorithm ($f$ single-exponential) for $tC_3\uplus C_4$; the case $H=C_4\uplus C_4$ is listed as open.
notes: No parenthetical attribution appears in the theorem header; treated as the paper authors' own question. It is the natural quasipolynomial companion to Question 1.
paper_title: Maximum Independent Set when excluding an induced minor: $K_1 + tK_2$ and $tC_3 \uplus C_4$
